name: 80s-90s Afrocentrism
summary: 80s-90s Afrocentrism was a design style, fashion trend, and cultural movement that occurred in the 1980s and 1990s and existed until its decline in the early 2000s.
description: 80s-90s Afrocentrism was a design style, fashion trend, and cultural movement that occurred in the 1980s and 1990s and existed until its decline in the early 2000s. This aesthetic was apart of the Pan Africanism and Afrocentric movements, promoting racial unity across the global Black diaspora and giving African people agency over their own history through disproving and correcting Eurocentric biases in philosophy, history, and education. This aesthetic is characterized by the usage of African prints and patterns, the Pan-African colors (green, yellow, black, and red), and the centering of Black people, cultures, and stories in popular media.
culturalContext: Key values (per the Aesthetics Wiki): Diversity, community, cultural reclamation, African centeredness

visualDNA.colour: Red, yellow, black, green, orange, purple

fashion.Overview: 80s-90s Afrocentrism prioritized Black-owned brands and African garments. Dashiki shirts, headwraps and kufi hats began to emerge in popular culture, and the usage of African prints and Pan African colors became popular alongside them. Afrocentric brands like Premier International and Cross Colours debuted during this time, as well as several Black-owned brands like FUBU and Karl Kani. Clothing with graphics of prominent Black political figures (like Malcolm X and MLK Jr.) and clothing repping HBCUs were also common. Gold jewelry was often worn to compliment the colors of the fashion and as a tie to African culture. Bomber jackets were popular, as were both sunglasses and fashion glasses.…
